taxes.base: Wages, salaries and pensions, withheld by the employer or the pension payer.
taxes.payer: Employees and pensioners; the employer withholds it.

details: The 13th and 14th monthly salaries are taxed at a flat 6%.

instruments.explanation: The largest direct tax: EUR 37.8 billion in 2025, 4.5% more than in 2024. The Länder and municipalities receive about a third of it.

taxes.base: Income of the self-employed, landlords and others who file a return.
taxes.payer: Individuals who file a return.

rate.headline: Same scale as the wage tax

instruments.explanation: Raised EUR 5.1 billion, against EUR 4.5 billion in the budget plan.

taxes.base: Dividends, interest and capital gains on securities, deducted by the bank or paying company.
taxes.payer: Investors; the bank deducts it.

rate.headline: 27.5% (25% on bank interest)
details: Dividends brought in EUR 3.7 billion and interest and other returns EUR 3.0 billion in 2025.

instruments.explanation: Revenue rose by 19% in 2025.

taxes.base: Profits of companies and other legal entities.
taxes.payer: Companies.

details: A minimum tax applies to loss-making companies.

instruments.explanation: Fell by 6% in 2025, the biggest fall of any federal tax.

taxes.base: The balance sheet of banks, above a threshold.
taxes.payer: Banks.

rate.headline: A rate on the balance sheet total
details: Raised sharply in 2025 as a consolidation measure.

instruments.explanation: Receipts more than tripled in 2025 after the levy was raised.

names.official: Other taxes on income and wealth (energy crisis contribution, foundation entry tax, land and forestry levy, land value levy)

taxes.base: Windfall profits of energy companies (the energy crisis contribution), the transfer of assets to foundations, agricultural and forestry businesses, and the value of building land.
taxes.payer: Energy firms, foundations, farms and landowners.

instruments.explanation: Energy crisis contribution EUR 367 million, foundation entry tax 54, land and forestry levy 33 and land value levy 6.

taxes.base: Supplies of goods and services and imports, with credit for tax on business purchases.
taxes.payer: Consumers; businesses charge it and remit the balance.

rate.headline: 20% standard; 13% and 10% reduced
details: 10% on food, books, rents and passenger transport; 13% on culture, wine sales by producers and some others.

instruments.explanation: The largest tax: EUR 40.2 billion. The Länder and municipalities receive about a third through the equalisation key.

taxes.base: Cigarettes and other tobacco products.
taxes.payer: Manufacturers and importers; passed on in the price.

rate.headline: A specific amount plus a share of the retail price

instruments.explanation: A mix of an amount per 1,000 cigarettes and a percentage of the retail price.

names.official: Alcohol taxes (alcohol tax, beer tax, sparkling wine and intermediate products tax)

taxes.base: Spirits, beer, sparkling wine and intermediate products, by volume.
taxes.payer: Producers and importers; passed on in the price.

rate.headline: Per hectolitre
details: Still wine is not taxed. Beer tax EUR 178.8 million, alcohol tax 145.1 and sparkling wine tax 1.8.

instruments.explanation: Three small excises grouped together.

taxes.base: Petrol, diesel, heating oil and other mineral oils, per 1,000 litres.
taxes.payer: Fuel suppliers; passed on at the pump.

instruments.explanation: Fell 3% in 2025; the national carbon pricing is charged on top.

names.official: Energy levies (Energieabgaben: electricity, natural gas and coal)

taxes.base: Electricity, natural gas and coal delivered to consumers.
taxes.payer: Energy suppliers; passed on in the bill.

rate.headline: Per kWh or cubic metre
details: The rates were cut to a minimum during the energy crisis and restored in 2025.

instruments.explanation: Receipts rose from EUR 33 million in 2024 to EUR 922 million in 2025 when the reduced rates ended.

names.official: National carbon pricing (national emissions trading for fuels outside the EU system)

taxes.base: The carbon content of fuels sold outside the EU emissions trading scheme: petrol, diesel, heating oil, gas and coal.
taxes.payer: Fuel suppliers; passed on in the price.

rate.headline: A fixed price per tonne of CO2 set by law
details: The price rises each year by law until the national scheme joins the EU trading system for buildings and transport.

instruments.explanation: Legally a trading scheme with a fixed certificate price, in practice a carbon tax; the federal accounts book it with the public charges.

taxes.base: New and imported cars and some vans at first registration, by CO2 emissions and price.
taxes.payer: The person who registers the vehicle.

instruments.explanation: A one-off tax at registration.

names.official: Motor vehicle tax and motor-related insurance tax (Kraftfahrzeugsteuer, motorbezogene Versicherungssteuer)

taxes.base: Ownership of a vehicle: the motor-related insurance tax is a monthly charge by engine power on cars; the motor vehicle tax applies to heavy vehicles.
taxes.payer: Vehicle owners, through the insurer or directly.

rate.headline: By engine power (cars); by weight (lorries)
details: The motor-related insurance tax brought in EUR 2.9 billion and the motor vehicle tax EUR 58 million.

instruments.explanation: Two annual vehicle taxes under two laws, grouped.

taxes.base: Premiums for non-life insurance such as home, liability and fire policies.
taxes.payer: Insurers, passed on in the premium.

rate.headline: 11% of the premium (lower for fire and some others)

instruments.explanation: Charged on most non-life insurance.

taxes.base: The value of land and buildings when ownership changes, including inheritance and gifts of property.
taxes.payer: The buyer or the receiver.

rate.headline: 3.5% (0.5%–2% within the family)
details: Within the family a stepped scale on the property value applies.

instruments.explanation: Revenue jumped by 17% in 2025 on a recovering property market. Austria has no inheritance tax; this tax applies to property that is inherited or given.

names.official: Levies under the Gambling Act (Abgaben nach dem Glücksspielgesetz)

taxes.base: Lottery and casino revenues, sports betting and slot machines.
taxes.payer: The licensed operators.

rate.headline: A share of stakes or gaming results

instruments.explanation: Revenue rose by 18% in 2025.

names.official: Other consumption and traffic taxes (digital tax, advertising tax, aviation levy, contaminated sites contribution)

taxes.base: Online advertising by large platforms, advertisements, passengers on flights from Austria and waste landfilled.
taxes.payer: Platforms, advertisers, airlines and waste operators.

rate.headline: Each has its own rate
details: Digital tax 5% of online advertising revenue; advertising tax 5% of advertising revenue.

instruments.explanation: Digital tax EUR 137 million, advertising tax 90, aviation levy 179 and contaminated sites contribution 70.

names.official: Stamp duties, administrative fees and other charges (Gebühren, Bundesverwaltungsabgaben und sonstige Abgaben)

taxes.base: Stamp duties on legal transactions, administrative fees of federal authorities and other charges and recoveries.
taxes.payer: Whoever requests the service or files the document.

rate.headline: Fixed amounts and percentages by transaction

instruments.explanation: The federal accounts report stamp duties (a tax) together with administrative fees (a charge for a service) and do not split the line.

names.official: Employers’ contribution to the family burdens equalisation fund (Dienstgeberbeitrag zum FLAF)

taxes.base: The wage bill of employers.
taxes.payer: Employers.

rate.headline: 3.7% of payroll
details: The chambers add a surcharge (DZ) that is included in the amount drawn.

instruments.explanation: Pays for family allowances and childcare benefits. The Länder and municipalities do not share it.

taxes.base: Gross earnings of employees up to a ceiling.
taxes.payer: Employees and employers (half each).

rate.headline: 6% of earnings (3% + 3%)
details: A reduced rate applies to low earnings.

instruments.explanation: Collected with the other social insurance contributions and paid to the Public Employment Service.

taxes.base: Gross earnings of employees up to a ceiling; income of the self-employed and farmers.
taxes.payer: Employees and employers; the self-employed pay in full.

rate.headline: 22.8% of earnings (10.25% + 12.55%)
details: The self-employed and farmers pay at their own rates.

instruments.explanation: The biggest social insurance contribution. The insurers also receive a federal guarantee payment (EUR 15.8 billion in 2025), which is not a contribution and is not counted.

taxes.base: Gross earnings of employees up to a ceiling; income of the self-employed; pensions.
taxes.payer: Employees and employers (almost equal shares); pensioners pay on their pensions.

rate.headline: About 7.65% of earnings
details: The employee pays 3.87% and the employer 3.78% for workers in the general scheme.

instruments.explanation: Funds the health insurance carriers; in 2025 they expect a combined deficit of EUR 511 million.

taxes.base: Gross earnings of employees up to a ceiling.
taxes.payer: Employers.

instruments.explanation: Pays for work accidents and occupational diseases.

taxes.base: The wage bill of businesses in the municipality.
taxes.payer: Employers.

instruments.explanation: The main own tax of the municipalities, paid to the municipality where the employer has its establishment.

taxes.base: Land and buildings, on the (very old) unit value set by the tax office.
taxes.payer: Owners.

rate.headline: A federal tax rate on the unit value, times a municipal multiplier
details: Municipalities may set the multiplier (Hebesatz) up to 500%.

instruments.explanation: A small tax because the unit values date from 1973.
